title: Two speeds of thought
text: Much of your mental life is run by a quiet, tireless assistant. Psychologists describe two {{1}} of thinking: System 1, fast, automatic and effortless — the machinery that {{2}} a face, finishes the phrase 'bread and…' or steers the car while you talk — and System 2, slow, deliberate and expensive, the one that {{3}} into gear for a tax form or a parallel park. The {{4}} of the arrangement is speed: we could not cross a road if every decision went to committee. The {{5}} is that the fast system answers before it understands. It sees patterns where there are none, {{6}} confidence it has not earned, and quietly swaps hard questions for easy ones — 'Is this person a good manager?' becomes 'Do I like their voice?'. System 2, the internal auditor, can {{7}} these snap conclusions before they take effect, but it is lazy: mobilising it takes effort, and it approves far too many of its assistant's hasty {{8}}. Knowing the two systems exist does not switch the fast one off. It does something better: it teaches you to notice the situations — tiredness, time pressure, easy fluency — where the auditor is most likely to be asleep at the desk, and to slow down on purpose.

gaps.explanation: 'two modes of thinking' — two styles of operating; mould = a shape or container, moat = a water-filled ditch, motif = a recurring design.
'the machinery that recognises a face' — identifies it instantly; reconcile = make peace between, recount = tell again.
'shifts into gear' — the standard verb with gears; shove = push roughly, shrug = raise the shoulders.
'The point of the arrangement is speed' — its purpose and justification; pore = a skin opening, or to pore over = study closely.
'The catch is that…' — the idiom for a hidden drawback; cache = a hidden store, caste = a social rank.
'displays confidence it has not earned' — shows it openly; displace = move something from its place, dissect = cut up for study.
'System 2 can veto these snap conclusions' — formally block them; vent = release pressure, veil = cover.
'approves too many of its assistant's hasty judgements' — snap assessments; junta = a military ruling group.
